youtube_title: Wanatah, Indiana: the 1901 robbery that failed and still broke the bank (Wanatah request)
youtube:
You asked for Wanatah! In late 1901, someone tried to rob the Wanatah Bank, a private bank owned by Julius Conitz. The attempt failed, but the news frightened many depositors and set off a run on the bank. On Dec. 12, 1901, two weeks after the attempt, the bank suspended business. On paper, Conitz had $91,000 in property, three times the $29,100 owed, and $40,000 of it was railroad stock. The Indianapolis Journal reported he couldn't turn his property into cash fast enough, so he turned everything he owned over to trustees, including the bank, three farms and his home, to pay creditors and depositors. Does your family know the rest of the story? Comment your town, and it could be next! #Wanatah #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; no picture of the 1901 bank building is known, so it is drawn generic. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: The Indianapolis Journal (Dec. 13, 1901, p. 3); The Saint Paul Globe (Dec. 13, 1901, p. 7) and Cameron County Press (Dec. 19, 1901, p. 6), the same wire story; Rand McNally Bankers' Directory (July 1900); via Chronicling America and the Historical Bank Runs database (finhist.com). More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history
